news.title: Iron ore sales to Asia soar
news.text: Economy up 1. The Iron Ore Mine owner collects $50.
news.logic: Owner of iron_ore_mine collects $50 from Bank.

news.title: Shoppers are spending again
news.text: Economy up 1.
news.logic: No money moves.

news.title: New suburbs planned: builders flat out
news.text: Economy up 1. Trades owners collect $20 per Trades business.
news.logic: Each player collects $20 x (trades businesses they own) from Bank.

news.title: Tourists flock back to WA
news.text: Economy up 1. Fun & Fitness owners collect $20 per business.
news.logic: Each player collects $20 x (fun_fitness businesses they own) from Bank.

news.title: Lithium rush for electric car batteries
news.text: Economy up 1. The Lithium Mine owner collects $50.
news.logic: Owner of lithium_mine collects $50 from Bank.

news.title: Government spends big on roads and rail
news.text: Economy up 1. Treasury builds the next Public Project now, borrowing if it must.
news.logic: Treasury builds the next unbuilt Public Project now ($300 to Bank), borrowing Bonds if short. Nothing extra if all 5 are built.

news.title: Record wheat harvest
news.text: Economy up 1. Food Shop owners collect $20 per Food Shop.
news.logic: Each player collects $20 x (food_shops businesses they own: Bakery, Butcher, Corner Deli; not the Supermarket) from Bank.

news.title: Businesses confident: new shops opening
news.text: Economy up 1.
news.logic: No money moves.

news.title: Overseas orders dry up
news.text: Economy down 1. Factory owners pay $20 per Factory.
news.logic: Each player pays $20 x (factories they own) to Bank.

news.title: Shoppers tighten their belts
news.text: Economy down 1.
news.logic: No money moves.

news.title: Banking crisis overseas
news.text: Economy down 2. Nobody can take a new loan until the next News card.
news.logic: Set flag noNewLoans = true. Clear it when the next News card is resolved.

news.title: Pandemic: shops shut for a month
news.text: Economy down 2. Treasury pays every player $50 support, borrowing if it must.
news.logic: Treasury pays $50 to every player, borrowing Bonds if short.

news.title: Trade war: new taxes on our exports
news.text: Economy down 1. Mine owners pay $30 per Mine.
news.logic: Each player pays $30 x (mines they own) to Bank.

news.title: Share market crash
news.text: Economy down 1. Every player loses $50 from their Super, if they have it.
news.logic: Each player's Super falls by min($50, their Super). That money goes from their Super pile to the Bank.

news.title: Quiet quarter: no big news
news.text: Nothing changes.
news.logic: Nothing happens.

news.title: Experts say steady as she goes
news.text: Nothing changes.
news.logic: Nothing happens.

news.title: Oil price shock
news.text: Transport owners pay $20 per transport business. Level 2: Prices up 1.
news.logic: Each player pays $20 x (transport businesses they own) to Bank.

news.title: Drought pushes up food prices
news.text: Takeaway owners pay $20 per Takeaway. Level 2: Prices up 1.
news.logic: Each player pays $20 x (takeaway businesses they own) to Bank.

news.title: Minimum wage goes up
news.text: Every business owner pays $10 per business. Level 2: Wages up 1.
news.logic: Each player pays $10 x (all businesses they own, including transport and sold utilities) to Bank.

news.title: Self-checkouts everywhere
news.text: The Cashier and the Retail Assistant lose their jobs.
news.logic: Players holding J03 Cashier or J01 Retail Assistant who are employed become looking for work (Volunteer card L12 may be handed in).

news.title: Robots in warehouses and kitchens
news.text: The Delivery Driver and the Kitchen Hand lose their jobs.
news.logic: Players holding J04 Delivery Driver or J02 Kitchen Hand who are employed become looking for work (L12 may be handed in).

news.title: Tech boom: skilled workers wanted
news.text: Every Skilled and Professional worker collects $30. Skilled and Professional players looking for work get their jobs back.
news.logic: First: every employed Skilled or Professional worker collects $30 from Bank. Then: every Skilled or Professional player looking for work becomes employed (they do not get the $30).

news.title: Australian dollar falls
news.text: Mine and Factory owners collect $20 per business, because our exports are cheaper overseas. Level 2: Prices up 1, because imports cost more.
news.logic: Each player collects $20 x (mines + factories they own) from Bank.

news.title: Bushfire emergency
news.text: Treasury pays $100 to the Bank for recovery, borrowing if it must. Market Stall and Fun & Fitness owners pay $20 per business.
news.logic: Treasury pays $100 to Bank (borrow if short). Each player pays $20 x (market_stalls + fun_fitness businesses they own) to Bank.

life.title: Car breaks down
life.text: Pay $60 to the Bank.
life.logic: Drawer pays $60 to Bank.

life.title: Cracked phone screen
life.text: Pay $40 to the Bank.
life.logic: Drawer pays $40 to Bank.

life.title: It's your birthday
life.text: Every player gives you $10.
life.logic: Every other player pays the drawer $10.

life.title: Sold your old bike online
life.text: Collect $30 from the Bank.
life.logic: Drawer collects $30 from Bank.

life.title: Tax refund
life.text: Collect $40 from Treasury.
life.logic: Drawer collects $40 from Treasury (borrow if short).

life.title: Sick for a week
life.text: Entry job: lose $50, because casual workers get no sick pay. Skilled or Professional: you get paid sick leave, so nothing happens.
life.logic: If drawer is employed in an Entry job: pays $50 to Bank. Otherwise nothing.

life.title: Promotion at work
life.text: If you have a job, collect $50 from the Bank.
life.logic: If drawer is employed: collects $50 from Bank.

life.title: Speeding fine
life.text: Pay $100 to Treasury.
life.logic: Drawer pays $100 to Treasury.

life.title: Scam text message
life.text: If you have more than $300 in cash, the scammer takes $100 (pay the Bank). Never click links in texts.
life.logic: Ask the drawer: more than $300 cash? Yes: pays $100 to Bank. Savings are safe.

life.title: Buy now, pay later trap
life.text: Pay $60 to the Bank: $50 for the shoes and a $10 late fee.
life.logic: Drawer pays $60 to Bank.

life.title: Cheaper phone plan
life.text: You shopped around. Collect $20 from the Bank.
life.logic: Drawer collects $20 from Bank.

life.title: Volunteer at the community garden
life.text: KEEP. Next time you lose your job, hand this in to get it back straight away. Someone gave you a reference.
life.logic: Drawer keeps it. The next time they would lose their job (any cause), offer to hand it in: job kept, card returns to the deck.

life.title: Move into a share house
life.text: KEEP. Pay $10 less living costs at every Payday.
life.logic: Drawer keeps it for the rest of the game: living costs -$10 at every Payday.

life.title: Rent goes up
life.text: Pay $40 to the Bank.
life.logic: Drawer pays $40 to Bank.

life.title: Free online course
life.text: KEEP. Hand this in to do TAFE with no fee.
life.logic: Drawer keeps it. When they enrol in TAFE, offer to hand it in: no fee. Card returns to the deck.

life.title: Dentist visit
life.text: Pay $80 to the Bank. Medicare does not cover most dental care.
life.logic: Drawer pays $80 to Bank.

life.title: Side hustle
life.text: You sell drawings online. Collect $40 from the Bank.
life.logic: Drawer collects $40 from Bank.

life.title: Broken arm
life.text: Medicare covers the hospital. Pay only $20 to the Bank. Without public health care this could cost thousands.
life.logic: Drawer pays $20 to Bank.

life.title: Insurance offer
life.text: Pay $30 to the Bank to KEEP this card, or put it back. It covers your next Car Crash or Fire card.
life.logic: Ask: buy insurance? Yes: drawer pays $30 to Bank and keeps the card. It cancels the next L20 Car Crash or M13 Fire payment, then returns to the deck.

life.title: Car crash
life.text: Pay $150 to the Bank, unless you hand in an Insurance card.
life.logic: Drawer pays $150 to Bank unless they hold L19: then hand it in and pay nothing.

market.title: Video goes viral
market.logic: Each player collects $30 x (takeaway they own) from Bank.

market.title: Health inspector visit
market.text: Takeaway owners pay $20 per Takeaway to Treasury.
market.logic: Each player pays $20 x (takeaway they own) to Treasury.

market.title: Equipment breaks down
market.text: You pay $20 to the Bank for each business you own.
market.logic: Drawer pays $20 x (all businesses they own) to Bank.

market.title: Suppliers raise prices
market.text: Food Shop and Takeaway owners pay $20 per business to the Bank.
market.logic: Each player pays $20 x (food_shops + takeaway they own) to Bank.

market.title: Big chain store opens nearby
market.text: Market Stall and Food Shop owners pay $20 per business to the Bank. Small shops lose customers.
market.logic: Each player pays $20 x (market_stalls + food_shops they own) to Bank.

market.title: Online shopping takes off
market.text: Clothing Store and Electronics Store owners pay $30 each. Transport owners collect $20 per transport business.
market.logic: Each player pays $30 x (clothing_store + electronics_store they own) to Bank. Each player collects $20 x (transport they own) from Bank.

market.title: Workplace safety fine
market.text: Factory and Mine owners pay $40 per business to Treasury.
market.logic: Each player pays $40 x (factories + mines they own) to Treasury. Law P15 in force: $20 instead.

market.title: Pollution clean-up
market.text: Factory and Mine owners pay $30 per business to Treasury. The river was polluted and someone has to pay to fix it.
market.logic: Each player pays $30 x (factories + mines they own) to Treasury. Law P15 in force: $15 instead.

market.title: Small business grant
market.text: If you own a Market Stall or Food Shop, collect $50 from Treasury.
market.logic: If drawer owns at least one market_stalls or food_shops business: collects $50 once from Treasury (borrow if short).

market.title: Staff shortage
market.text: Every business owner pays $10 per business to the Bank for overtime.
market.logic: Each player pays $10 x (all businesses they own) to Bank.

market.title: Big overseas order
market.logic: Each player collects $40 x (factories they own) from Bank.

market.title: Business course
market.text: You may add an Extra Site to one business now for half price.
market.logic: Optional: drawer picks one of their businesses with fewer than 2 Extra Sites (not transport or utilities) and adds a site for half its Extra Site cost, paid to Bank.

market.title: Fire!
market.text: If you own any business, pay $100 to the Bank, unless you hand in an Insurance card.
market.logic: If drawer owns any business: pays $100 to Bank unless they hold L19 (hand it in, pay nothing).

market.title: Bargain for sale
market.text: You may buy any business nobody owns for half its price.
market.logic: Optional: drawer picks any unowned business (not utilities) and buys it for half its price, paid to Bank.

market.title: Supply deal
market.text: Choose another player who owns a business. You both collect $30 from the Bank. Working together helps both of you.
market.logic: Drawer picks another player who owns at least one business. Both collect $30 from Bank. If nobody else owns a business, nothing happens.

market.title: ACCC investigation
market.text: Anyone who owns every business in an industry pays $100 to Treasury. Level 3: they must also set Standard prices until their next Payday.
market.logic: For each player and each industry (not utilities) where they own every business: pay $100 to Treasury. Level 3: those businesses are forced to Standard price until that owner's next Payday.

policy.title: Raise the minimum wage
policy.text: Entry workers take home $20 more. At Payday, business owners pay $10 per business.
policy.logic: Law. Employed Entry workers: take-home +$20 (from Bank). At each player's Payday: pay $10 x (all businesses they own) to Bank.

policy.title: Cut income tax
policy.text: Every worker takes home $10 more, and Treasury gets $10 less from each.
policy.logic: Law. Employed workers: take-home +$10 and tax -$10 (Bank pays the same total).

policy.title: Raise company tax
policy.logic: Law. Tax Time is $30 per business.

policy.title: Cut company tax
policy.logic: Law. Tax Time is $10 per business.

policy.title: Build it now
policy.text: Treasury builds the next Public Project now, borrowing if it must. This card then goes to the bottom of the deck instead of staying as a law.
policy.logic: One-off if passed: Treasury builds the next Public Project now (borrow if short). Not kept as a law.

policy.title: Carbon price
policy.text: At Payday, Factory and Mine owners pay $20 per business to Treasury. The Solar Panel Factory owner collects $20 instead.
policy.logic: Law. At each player's Payday: pay $20 x (factories + mines they own, excluding solar_factory) to Treasury; if they own solar_factory, collect $20 from Treasury.

policy.title: Sell the utilities
policy.text: Auction the Power Company and Water Company now, bidding from $100. Owners collect the $20 bills. They stay sold even if this law is later removed.
policy.logic: Law. Immediately auction power_company then water_company (min bid $100, winner pays Treasury; no bid = stays government). Owned utilities: lander pays owner $20; owner gets $20 profit at every Payday. Stay sold if the law is removed.

policy.title: Raise GST
policy.text: Every player pays $10 more living costs, and that $10 goes to Treasury.
policy.logic: Law. Living costs +$10 at every Payday; that $10 goes to Treasury, the rest to Bank.

policy.title: Tax on imports
policy.text: At Payday, Factory owners collect $20 per Factory. Living costs go up $10.
policy.logic: Law. At each player's Payday: collect $20 x (factories they own) from Bank. Living costs +$10 (to Bank).

policy.title: Cap food prices
policy.text: Food Shops and the Supermarket charge customers $10 less. Level 3: Budget price only.
policy.logic: Law. Food Shops and Supermarket customer prices -$10 (min $0). Level 3: these businesses can only charge Budget.

policy.title: Tax on big fortunes
policy.text: At Payday, anyone with more than $1,000 in cash and Savings pays $50 to Treasury.
policy.logic: Law. At each player's Payday ask: cash + Savings over $1,000? (app knows Savings, ask about cash) Yes: pay $50 to Treasury.

policy.title: Cut red tape
policy.text: Safety fine and Pollution clean-up cards cost half.
policy.logic: Law. M07 and M08 cost half.

policy.title: Free trade deal
policy.text: Living costs go down $10. At Payday, Factory owners pay $10 per Factory.
policy.logic: Law. Living costs -$10. At each player's Payday: pay $10 x (factories they own) to Bank.

startingLife.title: Family can help
startingLife.text: Start with $700. Your first TAFE or Uni course is free, with no HECS card.
startingLife.logic: Start cash $700. Their first TAFE or Uni enrolment has no fee and no HECS card.

startingLife.title: Grew up in a country town
startingLife.text: Start with $400. TAFE costs you $100 because you must travel.
startingLife.logic: Start cash $400. Their TAFE fee is $100 (unless TAFE is free for them).

startingLife.title: Family business
startingLife.text: Start with $300 and the Coffee Cart.
startingLife.logic: Start cash $300 and they own coffee_cart.

startingLife.title: Young carer
startingLife.text: Start with $300. Take home $20 less at every Payday because you work fewer hours.
startingLife.logic: Start cash $300. Take-home pay -$20 at every Payday while employed.

startingLife.title: Average start
startingLife.logic: Start cash $400. The physical deck has 3 copies of this card.
